observations.text: TIB-5460 is a Bug at Highest priority, currently in status 'QA Review', assigned to linhpt. The issue is self-contained: no parent, no subtasks, no issue links, no remote links.

The issue carries two distinct authority layers. The description (PO/report side) states the case, the dev-confirmed root cause and a one-part Solution ('Remove the device-info-based fallback ID and generate a random ID per browser'). Comment 51220 states a THREE-part fix, explicitly widening the described solution with 'Fix has three parts now'.

No Jira-native relation exists to read: issuelinks empty, no parent, no subtasks, no remote issue links. Superseded in part by OBS-INTAKE-04 - a related issue (TIB-5341) does exist and was read, but it was found through the QA rule library, not through Jira.

TIB-5341 ('Enhance security for public merchant routes and bypassable rate limits', Done) is the direct cause of TIB-5460: it added the server-fetched signed thumbmark with a 3s-timeout fallback to the old device fingerprint. There is NO Jira link between TIB-5341 and TIB-5460 in either direction.

assumptions.text: Comment 51220 is treated as the Dev implementation note because it self-describes implementation delta ('What changed', 'Fix has three parts now') and test preconditions. It is NOT labelled as a dev note in Jira, and its author (huyenntk) is also the issue reporter.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: If 51220 is a QA-authored test guide rather than a dev-confirmed implementation note, its three-part fix description and its numeric constants (8s timeout, 1 retry, 5 uploads/window, 5-min staging window) lose CONFIRMED_EXPECTED status and drop to INFERRED, which would remove the oracle for several planned checks.

unknowns.text: TIB-5460 does not state whether the soft-transition window from TIB-5341 (ValidateThumbmark still accepting the legacy unsigned format) is still open. The new random fallback ID is an unsigned value, so it can only be accepted by the server while that window is open.

side_a.claim: The fix is one change: remove device-info fallback ID, generate a random ID per browser. Fetching earlier is explicitly described as insufficient, i.e. as a workaround, not part of the fix.
side_a.quote: Remove the device-info-based fallback ID and generate a random ID per browser instead, so different visitors never share the same quota. Fetching the visitor ID earlier only reduces the chance of falling back (network loss, timeout, incognito); it does not eliminate the collision on its own.

side_b.claim: The fix has three parts: random fallback ID, fetch visitor ID at page load, and a more resilient fetch (timeout 3s to 8s, one retry on network error/5xx but not on 429).
side_b.quote: Fix has three parts now: 1. The fallback ID is random and unique per browser ... 2. The SDK fetches the visitor ID as soon as the page loads ... 3. The fetch itself is now more resilient: longer timeout (3s -> 8s) ... and one retry on a network error/5xx before giving up (not on a 429 ...).

conflicts.resolution: NOT_RESOLVED_BY_ORCHESTRATOR. Both sides kept per contract section 8. Reading them as compatible (comment 51220 is later and says 'now', implying scope grew after the description was written) is the most likely reading but is an inference, not a confirmation. Test scope below covers the union of both sides.

feature_hints: storefront image upload with AI effect
per-visitor + per-product hourly upload rate limit
thumbmark fetch timing, timeout and retry policy

object_hints.evidence_quote: To enforce the hourly upload limit, the SDK sends a "thumbmark" (visitor ID) with every upload so the backend knows which visitor's quota to count against.
object_hints.why: The entire code change is in the storefront SDK: fallback ID generation, fetch timing, timeout and retry are all SDK-side behaviour.

object_hints.evidence_quote: Rate limiting only applies to uploads that use an AI effect (Remove Background, AI Enhance/Image Filter, Text-to-Image, etc.). A plain upload with no effect is never limited, so pick a product/campaign field that has one of these effects turned on.
object_hints.why: The upload surface being limited is an artwork personalization field configured with an AI effect. The registry alias 'print effects' is not a literal match for 'AI effect', so this is inferred, not keyword-matched.
object_hints.caveat: Artwork is the surface the limit acts on, not a surface the code change edits. Relevant for applicability of upload/AI-effect checklists, not as an oracle for the fix itself.

object_hints.evidence_quote: Rate limiting only applies to uploads that use an AI effect (Remove Background, AI Enhance/Image Filter, Text-to-Image, etc.)
object_hints.why: Literal alias hit on 'Text-to-Image', but it appears only as one example in a list of AI effects. Included so the retriever can judge applicability; low confidence on purpose, must not drive scope on its own.

object_hints.evidence_quote: pick a product/campaign field that has one of these effects turned on
object_hints.why: Campaign appears only as the vehicle for test data setup (the campaign that owns the AI-effect field). It is a test-data dependency, not an impacted surface.
